passage.title: Rizq Foods Ltd
paras: Rizq Foods Ltd makes halal ready meals in a factory next to a motorway junction. It was started by the Rahman family twelve years ago. Six family members own all the shares and four of them work in the business.
The company borrowed £200,000 to build its factory. Supermarkets now want more of its meals and it needs £500,000 for a second production line. Its retained profit is about £250,000 a year.

One director wants to become a public limited company and sell shares to raise the money quickly. Another wants to stay private, keep control in the family, and build the new line over two years from profit.
passage.source: All businesses, people and figures in this case are fictional, made up for practice.

blocks.text: 'Rizq Foods is considering becoming a public limited company.' Justify whether it should. (9 marks)

frame.label: Because (use the data)
frame.prompt: Give a reason and develop it into a chain, using figures from the case.

frame.label: However (the other option)
frame.prompt: Give the strongest point for the other option and develop it.

frame.label: Overall, why my choice beats it
frame.prompt: Compare the two: why your option is better for THIS business.

markScheme.a: Stay Ltd (likely): the family keeps control; £500,000 could come from two years of £250,000 retained profit; going public costs about £150,000 and means publishing accounts. Become plc: raises the money quickly to meet the 18-month supermarket deadline, but shares can be bought by anyone, so control may be lost. Level 3 (7-9): a justified choice that uses the data, with developed chains of reasoning and a comparison showing why it beats the other option. Level 2 (4-6): reasons for the choice in context but little comparison. Level 1 (1-3): generic points.
